remaining_failures.item: R-01: child processes can change protected file modes and timestamps. The observed chmod and utime succeeded; content SHA-256 remained unchanged, but the requested mutation-prevention claim is broader than this boundary.
R-02: raw filesystem operations from arbitrary in-process Python skills are not prevented by the application-level and child-process controls.
General OS isolation, network/read/process restrictions, and resistance to same-privilege checkout owners are not claimed or established.
Repository-wide Ruff formatter check reports 18 files requiring formatting; lint and configured verification gates are separate.

evidence_boundary: Application policies deny tested direct, declared file-skill operations before dispatch; they do not confine arbitrary raw filesystem operations from malicious in-process Python.

The Linux child boundary blocks tested content/namespace writes and selected ownership/xattr syscalls; observed chmod and utime succeeded on protected files. These controls are not a general OS sandbox.

Baseline reproductions were run from the exact requested Result 001 commit 71464d365c41da9c74ed3f943d031b135a316beb; remediation child enforcement was observed on Linux x86_64, kernel 6.1.158+, Landlock ABI 2.
The amendment --by field is self-asserted and confirmation is not a digital signature or human identity proof.
A hash chain and in-repository bootstrap lock are not external trust anchors against a same-privilege writer.
The R-06 self-extension/promotion regression uses a disposable fixture with use_git=False; no Git commit from that simulated promotion is claimed.

baseline_requested_revision_environment.baseline_system_file_note: The 30-byte .ourob/system.jsonl payload was a disposable sentinel, not validated promotion history; evidence is for the missing path protection/check coverage, not semantic acceptance of that payload.
